The nature of the roots of \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\) is decided by the sign of the discriminant \(b^2 - 4ac\).

When \(b^2 - 4ac = 5\) : \(5 > 0\), so the roots are real and unequal (distinct and real).

When \(b^2 - 4ac = -5\) : \(-5 < 0\), so the roots are not real.

If the sum of the roots is \(\alpha + \beta\) and their product is \(\alpha\beta\), the equation is

\(x^2 - (\alpha + \beta)x + \alpha\beta = 0\)

Here \(\alpha + \beta = -7\) and \(\alpha\beta = 5\).

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 - (-7)x + 5 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 + 7x + 5 = 0\)

Comparing \(2x^2 - 4x - 3 = 0\) with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(a = 2\), \(b = -4\), \(c = -3\).

\(\alpha + \beta = -\dfrac{b}{a} = -\dfrac{-4}{2} = 2\)

\(\alpha \times \beta = \dfrac{c}{a} = \dfrac{-3}{2}\)

\(\sqrt{2}\,x^2 + 4x + 2\sqrt{2} = 0\)

Comparing with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(a = \sqrt{2}\), \(b = 4\), \(c = 2\sqrt{2}\)

\(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac = (4)^2 - 4 \times \sqrt{2} \times 2\sqrt{2} = 16 - 8 \times 2 = 16 - 16\)

\(\Delta = 0\)

\(x^2 - 4x + 4 = 0\)

Comparing with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(a = 1\), \(b = -4\), \(c = 4\)

\(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac = (-4)^2 - 4 \times 1 \times 4 = 16 - 16\)

\(\Delta = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(\Delta = 0\), so the roots of the equation are real and equal.

\(2y^2 - 7y + 2 = 0\)

Comparing with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(a = 2\), \(b = -7\), \(c = 2\)

\(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac = (-7)^2 - 4 \times 2 \times 2 = 49 - 16\)

\(\Delta = 33\)

\(\therefore\) \(\Delta > 0\), so the roots of the equation are real and unequal.

\(m^2 + 2m + 9 = 0\)

Comparing with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(a = 1\), \(b = 2\), \(c = 9\)

\(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac = (2)^2 - 4 \times 1 \times 9 = 4 - 36\)

\(\Delta = -32\)

\(\therefore\) \(\Delta < 0\), so the roots of the equation are not real.

The quadratic equation whose roots are \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) is \(x^2 - (\alpha + \beta)x + \alpha\beta = 0\).

Let \(\alpha = 0\) and \(\beta = 4\).

\(\alpha + \beta = 0 + 4 = 4\)

\(\alpha\beta = 0 \times 4 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) the equation is \(x^2 - 4x + 0 = 0\), that is \(x^2 - 4x = 0\).

The quadratic equation whose roots are \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) is \(x^2 - (\alpha + \beta)x + \alpha\beta = 0\).

Let \(\alpha = 3\) and \(\beta = -10\).

\(\alpha + \beta = 3 + (-10) = -7\)

\(\alpha\beta = 3 \times (-10) = -30\)

\(\therefore\) the equation is \(x^2 - (-7)x + (-30) = 0\), that is \(x^2 + 7x - 30 = 0\).

The quadratic equation whose roots are \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) is \(x^2 - (\alpha + \beta)x + \alpha\beta = 0\).

Let \(\alpha = \dfrac{1}{2}\) and \(\beta = -\dfrac{1}{2}\).

\(\alpha + \beta = \dfrac{1}{2} + \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 0\)

\(\alpha\beta = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = -\dfrac{1}{4}\)

\(\therefore\) the equation is \(x^2 - 0 \cdot x - \dfrac{1}{4} = 0\), that is \(x^2 - \dfrac{1}{4} = 0\).

The quadratic equation whose roots are \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) is \(x^2 - (\alpha + \beta)x + \alpha\beta = 0\).

Let \(\alpha = 2 - \sqrt{5}\) and \(\beta = 2 + \sqrt{5}\).

\(\alpha + \beta = (2 - \sqrt{5}) + (2 + \sqrt{5}) = 4\)

\(\alpha\beta = (2 - \sqrt{5})(2 + \sqrt{5}) = 2^2 - (\sqrt{5})^2 = 4 - 5 = -1\)

\(\therefore\) the equation is \(x^2 - 4x + (-1) = 0\), that is \(x^2 - 4x - 1 = 0\).

Comparing \(x^2 - 4kx + k + 3 = 0\) with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(a = 1\), \(b = -4k\), \(c = k + 3\).

\(\alpha + \beta = -\dfrac{b}{a} = 4k\)  and  \(\alpha\beta = \dfrac{c}{a} = k + 3\)

Given : sum of the roots is double their product.

\(\therefore\) \(4k = 2(k + 3)\)

\(\therefore\) \(4k = 2k + 6\)

\(\therefore\) \(2k = 6\)

\(\therefore\) \(k = 3\)

Comparing \(y^2 - 2y - 7 = 0\) with \(ay^2 + by + c = 0\), \(a = 1\), \(b = -2\), \(c = -7\).

\(\alpha + \beta = -\dfrac{b}{a} = 2\)  and  \(\alpha\beta = \dfrac{c}{a} = -7\)

\(\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = (\alpha + \beta)^2 - 2\alpha\beta\)

\(= (2)^2 - 2 \times (-7)\)

\(= 4 + 14\)

\(\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = 18\)

Comparing \(y^2 - 2y - 7 = 0\) with \(ay^2 + by + c = 0\), \(a = 1\), \(b = -2\), \(c = -7\).

\(\alpha + \beta = 2\)  and  \(\alpha\beta = -7\)

\(\alpha^3 + \beta^3 = (\alpha + \beta)^3 - 3\alpha\beta(\alpha + \beta)\)

\(= (2)^3 - 3 \times (-7) \times 2\)

\(= 8 + 42\)

\(\alpha^3 + \beta^3 = 50\)

Comparing \(3y^2 + ky + 12 = 0\) with \(ay^2 + by + c = 0\), \(a = 3\), \(b = k\), \(c = 12\).

The roots are real and equal, so \(b^2 - 4ac = 0\).

\(\therefore\) \(k^2 - 4 \times 3 \times 12 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(k^2 - 144 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(k^2 = 144\)

\(\therefore\) \(k = 12\) or \(k = -12\)

\(kx(x - 2) + 6 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(kx^2 - 2kx + 6 = 0\)

Comparing with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(a = k\), \(b = -2k\), \(c = 6\).

The roots are real and equal, so \(b^2 - 4ac = 0\).

\(\therefore\) \((-2k)^2 - 4 \times k \times 6 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(4k^2 - 24k = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(4k(k - 6) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(k = 0\) or \(k = 6\)

But if \(k = 0\) the equation becomes \(6 = 0\), which is not a quadratic equation at all (the coefficient \(a\) must be non-zero).

\(\therefore\) \(k = 6\)

Let Pragati's present age be \(x\) years.

\(\therefore\) her age 2 years ago was \((x - 2)\) years and her age 3 years hence will be \((x + 3)\) years.

From the given condition,

\((x - 2)(x + 3) = 84\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 + 3x - 2x - 6 = 84\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 + x - 90 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 + 10x - 9x - 90 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x(x + 10) - 9(x + 10) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((x + 10)(x - 9) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = -10\) or \(x = 9\)

But age is never negative, so \(x \neq -10\).

\(\therefore\) Pragati's present age is 9 years.

Let the two consecutive natural even numbers be \(x\) and \(x + 2\).

From the given condition,

\(x^2 + (x + 2)^2 = 244\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 + x^2 + 4x + 4 = 244\)

\(\therefore\) \(2x^2 + 4x - 240 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 + 2x - 120 = 0\)   (dividing throughout by 2)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 + 12x - 10x - 120 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x(x + 12) - 10(x + 12) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((x + 12)(x - 10) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = -12\) or \(x = 10\)

But the numbers are natural numbers, so \(x \neq -12\).

\(\therefore\) \(x = 10\) and \(x + 2 = 12\).

\(\therefore\) the numbers are 10 and 12.

Following the flow chart :

Let the number of trees in a column be \(x\).

\(\therefore\) the number of trees in a row \(= x + 5\).

Total number of trees \(= x(x + 5)\).

From the given condition,

\(x(x + 5) = 150\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 + 5x - 150 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 + 15x - 10x - 150 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x(x + 15) - 10(x + 15) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((x + 15)(x - 10) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = -15\) or \(x = 10\)

But the number of trees is never negative, so \(x \neq -15\).

\(\therefore\) \(x = 10\).

\(\therefore\) there are 10 trees in each column and \(10 + 5 = 15\) trees in each row.

Let Kishor's present age be \(x\) years.

\(\therefore\) Vivek's present age is \((x + 5)\) years.

From the given condition,

\(\dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{x + 5} = \dfrac{1}{6}\)

\(\therefore\) \(\dfrac{(x + 5) + x}{x(x + 5)} = \dfrac{1}{6}\)

\(\therefore\) \(6(2x + 5) = x^2 + 5x\)

\(\therefore\) \(12x + 30 = x^2 + 5x\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 - 7x - 30 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 - 10x + 3x - 30 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x(x - 10) + 3(x - 10) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((x - 10)(x + 3) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = 10\) or \(x = -3\)

But age is never negative, so \(x \neq -3\).

\(\therefore\) Kishor's present age is 10 years and Vivek's present age is \(10 + 5 = 15\) years.

Let Suyash's score in the first test be \(x\) marks.

\(\therefore\) his score in the second test is \((x + 10)\) marks.

From the given condition, 5 times the second score equals the square of the first score.

\(5(x + 10) = x^2\)

\(\therefore\) \(5x + 50 = x^2\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 - 5x - 50 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 - 10x + 5x - 50 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x(x - 10) + 5(x - 10) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((x - 10)(x + 5) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = 10\) or \(x = -5\)

But a score is never negative, so \(x \neq -5\).

\(\therefore\) his score in the first test is 10 marks.

Let the number of pots made in one day be \(x\).

\(\therefore\) the production cost of each pot is \((10x + 40)\) rupees.

Total production cost per day \(= x(10x + 40)\).

From the given condition,

\(x(10x + 40) = 600\)

\(\therefore\) \(10x^2 + 40x - 600 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 + 4x - 60 = 0\)   (dividing throughout by 10)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 + 10x - 6x - 60 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x(x + 10) - 6(x + 10) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((x + 10)(x - 6) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = -10\) or \(x = 6\)

But the number of pots is never negative, so \(x \neq -10\).

\(\therefore\) \(x = 6\), and the cost of each pot \(= 10(6) + 40 = 100\).

\(\therefore\) he makes 6 pots per day and the production cost of one pot is ₹ 100.

Let the speed of the water current be \(x\) km/hr.

Speed of the boat in still water is 12 km/hr.

\(\therefore\) downstream speed \(= (12 + x)\) km/hr and upstream speed \(= (12 - x)\) km/hr.

From the given condition, the total time for 36 km each way is 8 hours.

\(\dfrac{36}{12 + x} + \dfrac{36}{12 - x} = 8\)

\(\therefore\) \(36\left[\dfrac{(12 - x) + (12 + x)}{(12 + x)(12 - x)}\right] = 8\)

\(\therefore\) \(36 \times \dfrac{24}{144 - x^2} = 8\)

\(\therefore\) \(864 = 8(144 - x^2)\)

\(\therefore\) \(108 = 144 - x^2\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 = 36\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = 6\) or \(x = -6\)

But speed is never negative, so \(x \neq -6\).

\(\therefore\) the speed of the water current is 6 km/hr.

Let Nishu alone take \(x\) days to complete the work.

\(\therefore\) Pintu alone takes \((x + 6)\) days.

In one day Nishu does \(\dfrac{1}{x}\) of the work and Pintu does \(\dfrac{1}{x + 6}\) of it.

Working together they finish in 4 days, so in one day they do \(\dfrac{1}{4}\) of the work.

\(\dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{x + 6} = \dfrac{1}{4}\)

\(\therefore\) \(\dfrac{(x + 6) + x}{x(x + 6)} = \dfrac{1}{4}\)

\(\therefore\) \(4(2x + 6) = x^2 + 6x\)

\(\therefore\) \(8x + 24 = x^2 + 6x\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 - 2x - 24 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 - 6x + 4x - 24 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x(x - 6) + 4(x - 6) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((x - 6)(x + 4) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = 6\) or \(x = -4\)

But the number of days is never negative, so \(x \neq -4\).

\(\therefore\) Nishu alone takes 6 days and Pintu alone takes \(6 + 6 = 12\) days.

Let the divisor be \(x\) (a natural number).

\(\therefore\) the quotient is \((5x + 6)\), and the remainder is 1.

By the division algorithm, dividend \(=\) divisor \(\times\) quotient \(+\) remainder.

\(460 = x(5x + 6) + 1\)

\(\therefore\) \(5x^2 + 6x + 1 - 460 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(5x^2 + 6x - 459 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(5x^2 + 51x - 45x - 459 = 0\)   (since \(51 \times (-45) = -2295 = 5 \times (-459)\) and \(51 - 45 = 6\))

\(\therefore\) \(x(5x + 51) - 9(5x + 51) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((5x + 51)(x - 9) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = -\dfrac{51}{5}\) or \(x = 9\)

But the divisor is a natural number, so \(x \neq -\dfrac{51}{5}\).

\(\therefore\) the divisor is 9 and the quotient is \(5(9) + 6 = 51\).

(Check : \(9 \times 51 + 1 = 459 + 1 = 460\).)

From the figure, AB \(= x\), DC \(= 2x + 1\) and the height AM \(= x - 4\).

\(A(\square ABCD) = \dfrac{1}{2}(AB + CD) \times AM\)

\(33 = \dfrac{1}{2}(x + 2x + 1) \times (x - 4)\)

\(\therefore\) \(66 = (3x + 1)(x - 4)\)

\(\therefore\) \(66 = 3x^2 - 12x + x - 4\)

\(\therefore\) \(3x^2 - 11x - 70 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(3x^2 - 21x + 10x - 70 = 0\)   (since \(-21 \times 10 = -210 = 3 \times (-70)\) and \(-21 + 10 = -11\))

\(\therefore\) \(3x(x - 7) + 10(x - 7) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((3x + 10)(x - 7) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((3x + 10) = 0\) or \((x - 7) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = -\dfrac{10}{3}\) or \(x = 7\)

But length is never negative.

\(\therefore\) \(x \neq -\dfrac{10}{3}\)   \(\therefore\) \(x = 7\)

AB \(= x = 7\) cm, CD \(= 2x + 1 = 15\) cm, BC \(= x - 2 = 5\) cm, and AD \(=\) BC \(= 5\) cm (the figure marks AD and BC as equal).

(Check : the height is \(x - 4 = 3\) cm and the horizontal offset at each end is \(\dfrac{15 - 7}{2} = 4\) cm, so AD \(= \sqrt{4^2 + 3^2} = 5\) cm, which agrees.)

\(x^2 + 2x + 11 = 0\)

\(x\) is the only variable and its maximum index is 2, with \(a = 1 \neq 0\).

\(\therefore\) it is a quadratic equation.

\(x^2 - 2x + 5 = x^2\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 - x^2 - 2x + 5 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(-2x + 5 = 0\)

The \(x^2\) terms cancel, so the maximum index of the variable is 1.

\(\therefore\) it is not a quadratic equation.

\((x + 2)^2 = 2x^2\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 + 4x + 4 = 2x^2\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 - 4x - 4 = 0\)

\(x\) is the only variable and its maximum index is 2, with \(a = 1 \neq 0\).

\(\therefore\) it is a quadratic equation.

\(\sqrt{5}\,x^2 - x - \sqrt{5} = 0\)

Comparing with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(a = \sqrt{5}\), \(b = -1\), \(c = -\sqrt{5}\)

\(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac = (-1)^2 - 4 \times \sqrt{5} \times (-\sqrt{5}) = 1 + 4 \times 5 = 1 + 20\)

\(\Delta = 21\)

\(-2\) is a root of \(2x^2 + kx - 2 = 0\), so putting \(x = -2\) must satisfy the equation.

\(2(-2)^2 + k(-2) - 2 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(8 - 2k - 2 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(6 - 2k = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(2k = 6\)

\(\therefore\) \(k = 3\)

The equation whose roots are \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) is \(x^2 - (\alpha + \beta)x + \alpha\beta = 0\).

Let \(\alpha = 10\) and \(\beta = -10\).

\(\alpha + \beta = 10 + (-10) = 0\)

\(\alpha\beta = 10 \times (-10) = -100\)

\(\therefore\) the equation is \(x^2 - 0 \cdot x - 100 = 0\), that is \(x^2 - 100 = 0\).

The equation whose roots are \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) is \(x^2 - (\alpha + \beta)x + \alpha\beta = 0\).

Let \(\alpha = 1 - 3\sqrt{5}\) and \(\beta = 1 + 3\sqrt{5}\).

\(\alpha + \beta = (1 - 3\sqrt{5}) + (1 + 3\sqrt{5}) = 2\)

\(\alpha\beta = (1)^2 - (3\sqrt{5})^2 = 1 - 45 = -44\)

\(\therefore\) the equation is \(x^2 - 2x - 44 = 0\).

The equation whose roots are \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) is \(x^2 - (\alpha + \beta)x + \alpha\beta = 0\).

Let \(\alpha = 0\) and \(\beta = 7\).

\(\alpha + \beta = 0 + 7 = 7\)

\(\alpha\beta = 0 \times 7 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) the equation is \(x^2 - 7x + 0 = 0\), that is \(x^2 - 7x = 0\).

\(3x^2 - 5x + 7 = 0\)

Comparing with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(a = 3\), \(b = -5\), \(c = 7\)

\(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac = (-5)^2 - 4 \times 3 \times 7 = 25 - 84\)

\(\Delta = -59\)

\(\therefore\) \(\Delta < 0\), so the roots of the equation are not real.

\(\sqrt{3}\,x^2 + \sqrt{2}\,x - 2\sqrt{3} = 0\)

Comparing with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(a = \sqrt{3}\), \(b = \sqrt{2}\), \(c = -2\sqrt{3}\)

\(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac = (\sqrt{2})^2 - 4 \times \sqrt{3} \times (-2\sqrt{3}) = 2 + 8 \times 3 = 2 + 24\)

\(\Delta = 26\)

\(\therefore\) \(\Delta > 0\), so the roots of the equation are real and unequal.

\(m^2 - 2m + 1 = 0\)

Comparing with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(a = 1\), \(b = -2\), \(c = 1\)

\(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac = (-2)^2 - 4 \times 1 \times 1 = 4 - 4\)

\(\Delta = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(\Delta = 0\), so the roots of the equation are real and equal.

\(\dfrac{1}{x + 5} = \dfrac{1}{x^2}\)

Cross-multiplying (note \(x \neq 0\) and \(x \neq -5\)),

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 = x + 5\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 - x - 5 = 0\)

Comparing with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(a = 1\), \(b = -1\), \(c = -5\)

\(b^2 - 4ac = (-1)^2 - 4 \times 1 \times (-5) = 1 + 20 = 21\)

\(x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} = \dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{21}}{2}\)

\(\therefore\) \(\dfrac{1 + \sqrt{21}}{2}\) and \(\dfrac{1 - \sqrt{21}}{2}\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(x^2 - \dfrac{3x}{10} - \dfrac{1}{10} = 0\)

Multiplying throughout by 10,

\(\therefore\) \(10x^2 - 3x - 1 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(10x^2 - 5x + 2x - 1 = 0\)   (since \(-5 \times 2 = -10 = 10 \times (-1)\) and \(-5 + 2 = -3\))

\(\therefore\) \(5x(2x - 1) + 1(2x - 1) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((2x - 1)(5x + 1) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = \dfrac{1}{2}\) or \(x = -\dfrac{1}{5}\)

\(\therefore\) \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) and \(-\dfrac{1}{5}\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\((2x + 3)^2 = 25\)

\(\therefore\) \(2x + 3 = 5\) or \(2x + 3 = -5\)

\(\therefore\) \(2x = 2\) or \(2x = -8\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = 1\) or \(x = -4\)

\(\therefore\) 1 and \(-4\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(m^2 + 5m + 5 = 0\)

Comparing with \(am^2 + bm + c = 0\), \(a = 1\), \(b = 5\), \(c = 5\)

\(b^2 - 4ac = (5)^2 - 4 \times 1 \times 5 = 25 - 20 = 5\)

\(m = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} = \dfrac{-5 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2}\)

\(\therefore\) \(\dfrac{-5 + \sqrt{5}}{2}\) and \(\dfrac{-5 - \sqrt{5}}{2}\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\(5m^2 + 2m + 1 = 0\)

Comparing with \(am^2 + bm + c = 0\), \(a = 5\), \(b = 2\), \(c = 1\)

\(b^2 - 4ac = (2)^2 - 4 \times 5 \times 1 = 4 - 20 = -16\)

\(m = \dfrac{-2 \pm \sqrt{-16}}{2 \times 5}\)

But \(\sqrt{-16}\) is not a real number.

\(\therefore\) the roots of the equation are not real.

\(x^2 - 4x - 3 = 0\)

Comparing with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(a = 1\), \(b = -4\), \(c = -3\)

\(b^2 - 4ac = (-4)^2 - 4 \times 1 \times (-3) = 16 + 12 = 28\)

\(x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} = \dfrac{4 \pm \sqrt{28}}{2} = \dfrac{4 \pm 2\sqrt{7}}{2} = 2 \pm \sqrt{7}\)

\(\therefore\) \((2 + \sqrt{7})\) and \((2 - \sqrt{7})\) are the roots of the given quadratic equation.

\((m - 12)x^2 + 2(m - 12)x + 2 = 0\)

Comparing with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(a = m - 12\), \(b = 2(m - 12)\), \(c = 2\).

The roots are real and equal, so \(b^2 - 4ac = 0\).

\(\therefore\) \([2(m - 12)]^2 - 4(m - 12)(2) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(4(m - 12)^2 - 8(m - 12) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(4(m - 12)[(m - 12) - 2] = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(4(m - 12)(m - 14) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(m = 12\) or \(m = 14\)

But if \(m = 12\) then \(a = 0\) and the equation becomes \(2 = 0\), which is not a quadratic equation at all.

\(\therefore\) \(m = 14\)

Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be the two roots.

Given : \(\alpha + \beta = 5\) and \(\alpha^3 + \beta^3 = 35\).

\(\alpha^3 + \beta^3 = (\alpha + \beta)^3 - 3\alpha\beta(\alpha + \beta)\)

\(\therefore\) \(35 = (5)^3 - 3\alpha\beta(5)\)

\(\therefore\) \(35 = 125 - 15\alpha\beta\)

\(\therefore\) \(15\alpha\beta = 90\)

\(\therefore\) \(\alpha\beta = 6\)

The equation is \(x^2 - (\alpha + \beta)x + \alpha\beta = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0\)

Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be the roots of \(2x^2 + 2(p + q)x + p^2 + q^2 = 0\).

\(\alpha + \beta = -\dfrac{2(p + q)}{2} = -(p + q)\)  and  \(\alpha\beta = \dfrac{p^2 + q^2}{2}\)

The required roots are \((\alpha + \beta)^2\) and \((\alpha - \beta)^2\).

\((\alpha + \beta)^2 = (p + q)^2\)

\((\alpha - \beta)^2 = (\alpha + \beta)^2 - 4\alpha\beta = (p + q)^2 - 2(p^2 + q^2)\)

\(= p^2 + 2pq + q^2 - 2p^2 - 2q^2 = -(p - q)^2\)

Sum of the required roots \(= (p + q)^2 - (p - q)^2 = 4pq\)

Product of the required roots \(= (p + q)^2 \times \left[-(p - q)^2\right] = -\left[(p + q)(p - q)\right]^2 = -(p^2 - q^2)^2\)

\(\therefore\) the required equation is \(x^2 - 4pqx - (p^2 - q^2)^2 = 0\).

Let the amount Sagar possesses be ₹ \(x\).

\(\therefore\) Mukund possesses ₹ \((x + 50)\).

From the given condition,

\(x(x + 50) = 15000\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 + 50x - 15000 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 + 150x - 100x - 15000 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x(x + 150) - 100(x + 150) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((x + 150)(x - 100) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = -150\) or \(x = 100\)

But an amount possessed is never negative, so \(x \neq -150\).

\(\therefore\) Sagar has ₹ 100 and Mukund has ₹ 150.

Let the greater number be \(x\) and the smaller number be \(y\).

From the given conditions,

\(x^2 - y^2 = 120\) ... (I)  and  \(y^2 = 2x\) ... (II)

Substituting (II) in (I),

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 - 2x = 120\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 - 2x - 120 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 - 12x + 10x - 120 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x(x - 12) + 10(x - 12) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((x - 12)(x + 10) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = 12\) or \(x = -10\)

If \(x = -10\) then \(y^2 = 2(-10) = -20\), which has no real solution, so that value is rejected.

\(\therefore\) \(x = 12\) and \(y^2 = 24\), so \(y = \sqrt{24}\) or \(y = -\sqrt{24}\).

\(\therefore\) the numbers are 12 and \(\sqrt{24}\), or 12 and \(-\sqrt{24}\).

Let the number of students be \(x\).

Each student then gets \(\dfrac{540}{x}\) oranges; with 30 more students each would get \(\dfrac{540}{x + 30}\) oranges.

From the given condition,

\(\dfrac{540}{x} - \dfrac{540}{x + 30} = 3\)

\(\therefore\) \(540\left[\dfrac{(x + 30) - x}{x(x + 30)}\right] = 3\)

\(\therefore\) \(540 \times 30 = 3x(x + 30)\)

\(\therefore\) \(16200 = 3x^2 + 90x\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 + 30x - 5400 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 + 90x - 60x - 5400 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x(x + 90) - 60(x + 90) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((x + 90)(x - 60) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = -90\) or \(x = 60\)

But the number of students is never negative, so \(x \neq -90\).

\(\therefore\) the number of students is 60.

Let the breadth of the farm be \(x\) metre.

\(\therefore\) the length of the farm is \((2x + 10)\) metre and the side of the pond is \(\dfrac{x}{3}\) metre.

Area of the farm \(= x(2x + 10)\); area of the pond \(= \left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)^2 = \dfrac{x^2}{9}\).

From the given condition, the area of the farm is 20 times the area of the pond.

\(x(2x + 10) = 20 \times \dfrac{x^2}{9}\)

\(\therefore\) \(9x(2x + 10) = 20x^2\)

\(\therefore\) \(18x^2 + 90x = 20x^2\)

\(\therefore\) \(2x^2 - 90x = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(2x(x - 45) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = 0\) or \(x = 45\)

But a breadth of 0 is impossible, so \(x \neq 0\).

\(\therefore\) breadth of the farm is 45 m, length is \(2(45) + 10 = 100\) m, and the side of the pond is \(\dfrac{45}{3} = 15\) m.

Let the larger tap alone take \(x\) hours to fill the tank.

\(\therefore\) the smaller tap alone takes \((x + 3)\) hours.

In one hour the larger tap fills \(\dfrac{1}{x}\) of the tank and the smaller fills \(\dfrac{1}{x + 3}\) of it.

Both together fill the tank in 2 hours, so in one hour they fill \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) of it.

\(\dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{x + 3} = \dfrac{1}{2}\)

\(\therefore\) \(\dfrac{(x + 3) + x}{x(x + 3)} = \dfrac{1}{2}\)

\(\therefore\) \(2(2x + 3) = x^2 + 3x\)

\(\therefore\) \(4x + 6 = x^2 + 3x\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 - x - 6 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x^2 - 3x + 2x - 6 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x(x - 3) + 2(x - 3) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((x - 3)(x + 2) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(x = 3\) or \(x = -2\)

But time is never negative, so \(x \neq -2\).

\(\therefore\) the larger tap takes 3 hours and the smaller tap takes \(3 + 3 = 6\) hours to fill the tank.
